## Codex runtime mapping

This workflow depends on `cursor-how`, `cursor-why` when rationale matters, and `cursor-arena` for structural alternatives. The generated `cursor-how`/`cursor-why` mirrors and their relevant references have been read in a bounded native follow-up; the receipts preserve paths, outputs, nulls and gaps. Resolve exact installed names before invocation; a published mirror and an observed read/role-flow are not proof of automatic availability or triggering. In the observed native path, candidate delegates used `collaboration.spawn_agent` with `agent_type=general-worker`, the cross-judge used `agent_type=reviewer`, and the failed-hypothesis redesign used `agent_type=planner`; these native roles are capability mappings, not proof of the upstream Cursor runner slugs or automatic trigger. Native model and effort selection follows the standing `model-capability-router`; invocation metadata and worker self-report must be recorded separately. The coordinator owns design synthesis, implementation and re-design when the sketch fails.
codex_rule: Respect native Codex model/effort, permissions and actual tool availability; no automatic Cursor runtime equivalence.

proof: Pinned source hashes and deterministic build are static provenance. A disposable native run launched two separate general-worker candidate packages, a reviewer cross-judge, and a planner redesign after a hypothesis failed; a later read-only native how/why follow-up read the generated mirrors and relevant references and recorded Ground/Scrap receipts with explicit nulls and gaps. The coordinator then implemented the synthesized contract in a disposable runtime, observed a revision-only drift failure, corrected it, and reran the runtime scenarios plus a repo-owned behavioral fixture test. The exact native agent types and requested profile invocation metadata are recorded in the companion report, while worker completion messages are self-reports. Automatic trigger, external why connector coverage, upstream Cursor runner equivalence, production implementation, and end-to-end host behavior remain unproven.
